sections.content: You know *soler* + infinitive from B1 Unit 5: in the imperfect it means "used to" (*solíamos reunirnos*). It is the natural way to describe a pattern in politics, how things usually went in those decades. *Solía* goes with one person and *solían* with several.

items.spanish: Los presidentes solían gobernar poco tiempo.
items.english: Presidents used to govern for a short time.

items.spanish: Un oficial solía escribir un plan y pedir apoyo a otros soldados.
items.english: An officer used to write a plan and ask other soldiers for support.

items.spanish: Santa Anna solía llegar al poder con el apoyo del ejército.
items.english: Santa Anna used to come to power with the army's support.

items.spanish: Los caudillos solían tener más fuerza que los gobiernos débiles.
items.english: Caudillos used to be stronger than weak governments.

sections.content: *Soler* is followed by an infinitive (*solían gobernar*) and not by another conjugated verb. It describes a habit, not one event: for one event use the preterite (*Santa Anna llegó al poder en una ocasión*).
